summary.intent: Fix DatePicker showing the day before the selected date for users in timezones ahead of UTC (issue #9129), and add the widget's first Selenium integration tests.
summary.issue_fit: Partial. Issue #9129 (supplied in the PR packet) is fixed: a picked date now displays correctly in UTC+ zones. But the same change shifts server-supplied dates back a day in UTC- zones.
summary.coverage: Both changed files reviewed against the full merge-base diff, plus the Python `Date` property and JSON date serialization. Base `main` was supplied by the caller. The untracked `.mcp.json` in the clone is outside the committed range and was not reviewed.
check_details: Reviewer ran a node reproduction at head 36549bca3a63d581f7b68d08054a7813c1e6a499 (`TZ=<zone> node unlocal.js`, verbatim copies of the base and head `_unlocal_date`), exit 0. America/Los_Angeles and America/New_York: UTC-midnight Sep 20 renders as base Fri Sep 20, head Thu Sep 19. Europe/Paris: 'Mon Sep 16 2019' renders as base Sun Sep 15, head Mon Sep 16.
Could not run the added Selenium tests in `tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py`: no browser, Selenium or network was available. They were settled by tracing the code instead.

findings.title: Stop shifting server-supplied dates back a day in UTC- timezones
findings.trigger: Python serializes `DatePicker.value`, `min_date` and `max_date` as milliseconds at UTC midnight (`bokeh/util/serialization.py:181-183`). The new lines subtract `getTimezoneOffset()` unconditionally, and in a browser west of UTC that offset is positive, so the instant moves into the previous UTC day.
findings.impact: Users in the Americas see `date(2019, 9, 20)` shown as Thu Sep 19, `min_date` allows one extra earlier day, and `max_date=date.today()` disables today. The merge-base rendered all three correctly.
findings.change: Apply the offset only to the local-midnight `toDateString()` strings that `_on_select` writes. Keep reading numeric timestamps by their UTC date, for example `typeof v == "number"` → `new Date(d.getUTCFullYear(), d.getUTCMonth(), d.getUTCDate())`.
findings.source: Issue #9129 via the supplied PR packet; commit 472e477.

findings.title: Exercise the date display under a non-UTC browser timezone
findings.trigger: All three new tests run only in the runner's timezone, and the CI configuration sets no `TZ`. With a UTC browser, the merge-base `_unlocal_date` already displays both the initial Sep 20 and the picked 'Mon Sep 16 2019' correctly.
findings.impact: The tests pass at the merge-base and at head, so they guard neither the issue #9129 fix nor the UTC- regression above.
findings.change: Run `test_js_on_change_executes` with an assertion on the initial displayed date under one UTC+ and one UTC- browser timezone (for example, by setting `TZ` for the driver process), or file the follow-up issue the maintainer suggested.
